newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: Zimbabwe shares surge to record high on sentiment.
newsitem.headline: Zimbabwe shares surge to record high on sentiment.

text.p: Zimbabwe's main industrial share index surged over 66 points to a new record high on Wednesday, fired by strong investor sentiment and static rates on the rival local money market, brokers said.
"There are a number of reasons why the markey is bullish. The main one is that there is strong investor confidence, especially in the future of some select companies," one broker said.

"The other is that interest rates are not moving on the other market where local investors are normally very active," he said of the local money market where short-term interest rates have been steady at around 25 percent for weeks.
"These two factors are likely to last for a while and in the process to benefit the stock market," he added.

The Zimbabwe Stock Exchange's 57-share industrial index jumped 66.43 points to 11,742.28 following some big gains in several counters, including Zimbabwe Sugar Refineries ZSR.ZI, which traded 45 cents up at 2,300, hotel group ZIMSUN, 20 cents higher at 500, and pharmaceutical group Caps, which surged 190 cents to 3,700.

The secondary seven-share mining index climbed 28.07 points to close at 838.43 on Wednesday, boosted by a 75-cent rise in heavyweight counter Wankie Colliery. Wankie, which gained 30 cents on Tuesday, traded at 725 cents.
